english: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers such that $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{(1+ax)e^{x}-1-bx}{x^{3}}$ exists and is a finite real number. Then the value of $ab$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $a$ तथा $b$ ऐसी वास्तविक संख्याएँ हैं कि $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{(1+ax)e^{x}-1-bx}{x^{3}}$ का अस्तित्व है तथा यह एक परिमित वास्तविक संख्या है। तब $ab$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Finite limit $\Rightarrow$ coefficients of $x$ and $x^{2}$ vanish: $a=-\dfrac12$, $b=1+a=\dfrac12$ (the limit is then $-\dfrac1{12}$)
solution_full: $\dfrac{N(x)}{x^{3}}=\dfrac{1+a-b}{x^{2}}+\dfrac{\frac12+a}{x}+\left(\dfrac{1}{6}+\dfrac{a}{2}\right)+O(x)$. If $1+a-b\neq0$ the quotient is unbounded; if $1+a-b=0$ but $\dfrac{1}{2}+a\neq0$, it is still unbounded. So both coefficients must vanish.
$\dfrac{1}{2}+a=0\Rightarrow a=-\dfrac{1}{2}$, and $b=1+a=\dfrac{1}{2}$. Then the limit equals $\dfrac{1}{6}-\dfrac{1}{4}=-\dfrac{1}{12}$, which is finite, so these values work and are the only ones.
originality_note: New: the condition says that (1 + ax)e^x agrees with the line 1 + bx up to the x^2 term, so a and b are read off from two vanishing coefficients (way 5). Closest known: finite-limit conditions such as (a sin x - bx)/x^3 or (a + b cos x)/x^2. Different because: the unknown multiplies the exponential, so a appears in two coefficients and the order of elimination matters.
blueprint_concepts: Determining unknown constants from a given limit value

concept_use.Determining unknown constants from a giv: A finite limit forces the coefficients of x and x^2 in the numerator to vanish, giving a = -1/2 and b = 1/2.

key_step: Expanding (1 + ax)e^x to third order and setting the x and x^2 coefficients to zero.
justification: Standard expansion with two coefficient conditions; routine multi-step, numerical format. L2, near 2025-P2-Q1 (L2).
